event.label: Borrell’s warning about a nuclear attack
event.description: Three articles report Josep Borrell’s October 13 warning about the Western response if Russia used nuclear weapons against Ukraine. The graph separates a reported warning from an actual attack or verified military capability.

topics.label: How strong would the response be?

topics.label: Would the response use nuclear weapons?

topics.label: How serious is the warning?

evidence.quote: Putin is probably not bluffing when he talks about his nuclear threats…
evidence.paraphrase: Borrell warns that Western forces could destroy Russia’s army if Russia attacked Ukraine with nuclear weapons.
evidence.supporting_sentence:
Putin is probably not bluffing when he talks about his nuclear threats against Ukraine, but neither is the west bluffing when he says that the Russian military will be annihilated by non-nuclear means in the event of any Russian nuclear attack against Ukraine.
As reported by Censor.NET with reference to Ukrinform, EU High Representative Josep Borrell stated this.
"Now there is a nuclear threat, and Putin says he's not bluffing. Well, he can't afford to bluff. And it should be clear that the people who support Ukraine, the European Union and its member states, the United States and NATO - they are also not bluffing. Any attack against Ukraine will find its response, not a nuclear response, but such a powerful one that, from a military point of view, the Russian army will be annihilated (destroyed. - Ed.), and Putin will not need to bluff", - he said.
evidence.source_basis: Saved recovered article text in the user’s DNIPRO workspace.

claims.uncertainty: The P3 English quote says "Any attack"; P1 and the surrounding nuclear discussion supply the nuclear condition. Do not broaden this into a threat after every conventional attack.

edges.label: Same conditional warning
edges.reason: Both report Borrell warning of a response strong enough to destroy Russia’s army after Russian nuclear use. These reports rely on the same original statement.
edges.caveat: Both reports repeat Borrell’s warning. Their shared source provides no separate evidence about military capability or a future response.

edges.label: Same warning, different language
edges.reason: Both carry Borrell’s claim about the power of a future response; Izvestia reports it in Russian. These reports rely on the same original statement.
edges.caveat: Both reports repeat Borrell’s warning. Their shared source provides no separate evidence about military capability or a future response.

edges.label: Same non-nuclear limit
edges.reason: Both report Borrell specifying that the response would not use nuclear weapons. These reports rely on the same original statement.
edges.caveat: Both reports repeat Borrell’s warning. Their shared source provides no separate evidence about military capability or a future response.

edges.label: Same stated limit
edges.reason: The articles agree on what Borrell says about non-nuclear means. These reports rely on the same original statement.
edges.caveat: Both reports repeat Borrell’s warning. Their shared source provides no separate evidence about military capability or a future response.

edges.label: Same message of resolve
edges.reason: Both attribute the statement that Western supporters are not bluffing to Borrell. These reports rely on the same original statement.
edges.caveat: Both reports repeat Borrell’s warning. Their shared source provides no separate evidence about military capability or a future response.

edges.label: Same speaker, same message
edges.reason: Censor and Kyiv Independent repeat Borrell’s message that the warning is serious. These reports rely on the same original statement.
edges.caveat: Both reports repeat Borrell’s warning. Their shared source provides no separate evidence about military capability or a future response.

edges.label: France’s stated policy supports a limited part of the warning
edges.reason: Izvestia quotes Macron saying France would use no nuclear response to a Russian nuclear attack on Ukraine. That supplies one national policy position compatible with the non-nuclear response Borrell describes.
edges.caveat: Macron speaks for France. This is limited support from a national position within Borrell’s wider institutional description.
edges.support_scope: The French component of the broader Western non-nuclear response in KI02.
edges.direction_reason: I04 supplies the specified support for KI02.
edges.unsupported_parts: The position of every EU or NATO member or the action any state would actually take.

method.country_note: Outlet countries describe origin. Claimant countries describe an office, organization or stated residence, not assumed citizenship.
method.claim_type_note: A fact claim is a checkable statement, not a fact verified by this graph. Opinions, predictions, legal positions and promises are marked separately.
method.edge_note: Green arrows point from a supporting claim to the claim receiving support. Grey comparisons have no assigned direction. Solid red arrows point from a source claim to a target claim it is proposed to contradict. Red direction follows the analyst-assigned comparison order. Every proposed conflict retains its reasoning and scope limits for human review.
method.attention_note: Attention is a qualitative reading of the saved article, with paragraph locators; it is not a measured share of words.
method.endorsement_note: A quoted speaker’s view is separate from the article narrator’s view. No outlet-wide position is inferred from one article.
method.cleaning_note: Uses saved recovered text. Kyiv Independent later Most Popular / News Feed material is excluded; original paragraph numbers retained. FT wrapped lines are joined into logical paragraphs.
